name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but Democratic nominee Avila Chevalier heavily funded
Republican Jomo Williams shows no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The seat sits in a D+32 district, and the Democratic nominee has raised over $1.3 million with substantial outside support while the Republican reports no fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A surprise general-election polling miss or an unexpectedly funded Republican campaign could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 13th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Adriano Espaillat is not on the ballot after losing renomination, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Darializa Avila Chevalier enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised about $1.35 million and drawn roughly $1.9 million in outside support, alongside $1.5 million in outside spending against her.

Republican Jomo Williams reports no fundraising or cash on hand, leaving him badly outmatched in resources. No general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
